analyst_view.overall: A Monday-night Valencian relegation derby: Levante (18th, 11 points) host Elche (19th, 10 points), and the winner climbs out of the drop zone. Luís Castro has the whole squad available, with Manu Sánchez back from a hamstring injury and Axel Tape back from France U20 duty. Martín Anselmi's Elche miss Marc Aguado, Yago and Adam Boayar (only Houary is in the numbers), while Revivo trained normally, Cepeda is back from Chile and Lemar may only travel if ready to start; Elche have lost their last two without scoring and blanked in four of their last five league games, and have not won at Levante since 1993. Referee Francisco José Hernández Maeso (4.2 cards a game) is counted, but the numbers do not flag the derby or the relegation stakes.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, high for two bottom-three sides, and their momentum only trims Elche by about 1% despite four blanks in five league games. Elche still miss playmaker Marc Aguado, whom the numbers don't list, Anselmi admits his side waste their chances, and a tense six-pointer where neither can afford to lose tends to be cagey; a mild lean down to about 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners, 4.9 of them Levante's. Anselmi expects Levante to take the initiative at home and Elche's possession game with crosses already shows in their 31 corners in six games; the team news does not change that, so I keep 8.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards, including referee Hernández Maeso (about -12% for his 4.2 a game), which I don't size again, and Levante's light recent booking count. This is a regional derby and a direct relegation fight between sides a point apart, which the numbers do not flag, and Elche's players call it a must-win; such games usually bring more fouls and bookings, so a moderate lean up to about 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.5 shots and already add for both sides' recent shooting (Levante conceded 103 in six). Anselmi expects Levante to press and attack at home and Elche keep the ball, but a nervy six-pointer could slow it; nothing points clearly either way, so 29.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. Levante have a full squad with Iván Romero and Etta Eyong up front, and Elche's poor finishing lately is about conversion more than shots on target; that is close to the picture the numbers have, so 8.9.
